title: nested if !quit / if let Some could be one guard
description: The pending_sc dispatch block is: if !state.quit { if let Some(sc) = pending_sc.take() { ... } }. This double-nesting makes the quit guard appear more conditional than it is. Suggested rewrite: if !state.quit { if let Some(sc) = pending_sc.take() { ... } } — no structural change possible without an early-continue pattern, but the outer guard could be expressed as: pending_sc.take().filter(|_| !state.quit).map(|sc| handle_state_change(...)) — though that loses the await. The existing form is actually unavoidable for async, so this is a marginal observation.
